counterevidence_considered.description: All 24 ponds come from a single upland survey region, which could raise a spatial-clustering dependence concern; however, this is not repeated entry of the same independent unit into the row-independent procedure, and the description states no within-file grouping of ponds into clusters is recorded, so it does not establish the issue class under review.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: single survey region; no cluster/grouping column in the file

evidence.description: data/input.csv contains exactly 24 data rows and every pond_id (QP-01 through QP-24) is distinct, so no independent unit appears on more than one row entering the analysis.
The data description names pond_id as the independent-unit column, states one row is one pond surveyed a single time, and explicitly rules out repeat visits, replicate rows, or repeated codes.
evidence.observed_value: one row = one pond; pond_id unique; no repeat visits or replicate lines

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one abandoned quarry pond surveyed a single time, with one pooled water sample screened for great crested newt eDNA
Independent unit column: pond_id
One trial is: one row

Every pond is its own independent unit. There are no repeat visits, no split or
replicate samples written out as extra lines, and no grouping of ponds inside
larger clusters recorded in this file, so the rows can be treated as separate
observations of separate ponds.

evidence.description: The workflow actively enforces one entry per independent unit before running the row-independent Fisher exact test: it raises an error if any pond_id repeats, and cross_tabulate increments exactly one contingency-table cell per row.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate-pond guard present; one table increment per row

evidence.description: The report's selected result claims 24 independently surveyed ponds with counts 9/12 restored detected and 3/12 unrestored detected; manual recount of the 24 unique-pond rows reproduces exactly these counts and the stated Fisher two-sided p-value of 0.0391 for the table [[9,3],[3,9]], so the reported statistic is computed from one trial per unit.
evidence.observed_value: restored: 9 detected / 3 not; unrestored: 3 detected / 9 not; p = 0.0391 confirmed

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] A two-sided Fisher exact test on 24 independently surveyed quarry ponds returns p = 0.0391 with a sample odds ratio of 9.00; great crested newt eDNA was detected in 9 of 12 restored-shelf ponds (0.750) against 3 of 12 unrestored ponds (0.250).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by (1) scanning all 24 data rows of data/input.csv for any repeated pond_id or any column encoding visits, replicates, or subsamples that would put the same pond on multiple rows — none exist; (2) tracing workflow/analysis.py for any code path that could enter a pond more than once into the Fisher exact test (e.g., row duplication, per-replicate expansion, or double-counting in cross_tabulate) — each row increments exactly one cell once, and check_one_survey_per_pond would abort on duplicate pond_ids; and (3) recomputing the 2x2 table and Fisher two-sided p-value by hand from the unique-pond rows, which reproduces the reported 9/3 vs 3/9 table, odds ratio 9.00, and p = 0.0391. Every attempt to find a repeated independent-unit entry failed, so the issue class is not demonstrated.
